newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open firmer, sentiment upbeat.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open firmer, sentiment upbeat.

text.p: Singapore shares opened firmer on Monday with bargain huntingin selected blue chips and index- linked stocks, traders said.
"Sentiment is certainly up and we should see some short-term support. The market is oversold," a broker with a Singapore firm said.
Dealers said the buying of blue chips, which started last Friday, continued. A strong close on Wall Street on Friday also underpinned buying, they said.
The Straits Times industrial index climbed 14.46 points to 2,030.69 at 0216 GMT.
There were several early block trades which contributed to total market volume of 43.5 million shares with 147 gainers against 27 losers.
Property-based UIC Holdings was active with 1.8 million crossed at around Singapore $1.082. The counter was up three cents to S$1.10.
Block trades were also seen in HongKong Land, which firmed two cents to US$2.20, and in SIA foreign, which eased 10 cents to S$12.70.
Keppel Corp and SembCorp were firmer by 20 cents each to S$6.55 and S$6.60 respectively while Cycle & Carriage and ST Aerospace foreign were weaker.
